title: Air Traffic Control Services & Communications
description: Key concepts from AIM Chapter 4 covering ATC facilities, radio communications, transponder operations, and flight plans

cards.back:
ARTCC (Center): En route IFR control
TRACON (Approach): Terminal area control
Tower (Local): Airport traffic control
Ground: Taxiing aircraft
Clearance Delivery: IFR clearances
FSS: Briefings, flight plans, advisories

• Pilot weather briefings
• Flight plan filing/processing
• En route flight advisories (Flight Watch)
• Search and rescue initiation
• Assistance to lost/emergency aircraft
• Relay ATC clearances
• Broadcast weather and NOTAMs
• VFR Search and Rescue (SAR)

• Used at airports without operating tower
• May be UNICOM, MULTICOM, FSS, or tower frequency
• Published in Chart Supplement and on charts
• Self-announce position and intentions
• Key for see-and-avoid at non-towered airports

• 121.5: Emergency/guard frequency
• 122.0: FSS (en route)
• 122.2: FSS (local)
• 122.7, 122.8, 122.725, 122.975: UNICOM
• 122.9: MULTICOM (no tower, FSS, or UNICOM)
• 122.75: Air-to-air (private fixed wing)
• 123.0: UNICOM (towers operating)
• 123.025: Helicopter air-to-air

Contains:
• Airport/facility name
• Phonetic code (Alpha, Bravo...)
• Time (UTC)
• Weather (wind, visibility, sky, temp, dewpoint, altimeter)
• Instrument approach in use
• Runway in use
• NOTAMs/special information

Report code on initial contact!

'Have numbers' = Wind, runway, altimeter ONLY

'Information [Alpha] received' = Full ATIS broadcast

Using 'have numbers' doesn't confirm ATIS receipt - controller may need to provide additional info

7500: Hijacking
• '75 - taken alive'

7600: Communication failure
• '76 - need a fix' (radio)

7700: Emergency
• '77 - going to heaven'

1200: VFR (no ATC services)

Required in/above:
• Class A, B, C airspace
• Mode C veil (30 NM from Class B primary)
• Above 10,000 MSL (except ≤2,500 AGL)
• Within 10 NM of certain airports listed in Part 91

ADS-B Out also required in these areas (since 2020)

Required where Mode C is required PLUS:
• Class E at/above 3,000 MSL over Gulf of Mexico
• Within 12 NM of coastline

Must transmit:
• Position, altitude, velocity
• Aircraft identification
• NIC/NAC integrity parameters

Two types (mandatory service):

1. Terrain/Obstruction Alert:
• Aircraft in unsafe proximity to terrain/obstacles
• 'Low altitude alert, check your altitude immediately'

2. Aircraft Conflict Alert:
• Unsafe proximity to other aircraft
• TCAS-like ground-based detection

• Automated controller aid
• Alerts when Mode C aircraft below safe altitude
• Available for IFR aircraft
• VFR can REQUEST MSAW monitoring
• May not be available near borders (lack of terrain data)

Available at all radar facilities:
• Safety alerts (mandatory)
• Traffic advisories (workload permitting)
• Limited radar vectoring (workload permitting)
• Sequencing (where established)

NOT standard IFR separation - pilot must see and avoid!

Include:
1. Facility name
2. Aircraft callsign and type
3. Position
4. Altitude
5. Transponder code (if assigned)
6. Destination
7. 'Request VFR advisories' or 'flight following'

Service is workload permitting - may be denied

'Radar Contact':
• ATC has identified your aircraft
• Radar services begin

'Radar Service Terminated':
• No longer providing radar services
• VFR: Squawk 1200
• Resume own navigation/traffic avoidance

Auto-terminated when VFR aircraft lands at tower airport

Standard pattern: LEFT turns

Recommended entry:
• Enter at 45° to downwind
• At pattern altitude (usually 1,000 AGL)
• Avoid overflying airport

Right traffic: Indicated by 'RP' on charts, listed in Chart Supplement

All turns in direction of traffic pattern

1. Upwind: Parallel to runway, direction of landing
2. Crosswind: Perpendicular after departure
3. Downwind: Parallel to runway, opposite direction
4. Base: Turn from downwind toward runway
5. Final: Aligned with runway for landing

Departure: Crosswind at 300' below pattern altitude or ½ mile, or as directed

Formerly 'position and hold'

• Taxi onto runway, await takeoff clearance
• NOT cleared for takeoff!
• Used for traffic sequencing
• Be alert for takeoff clearance
• If no clearance in reasonable time, query ATC

'Cleared for takeoff' = begin takeoff roll

• Land and stop before intersection/point
• ATC provides available landing distance
• Pilot must determine if acceptable
• Part 91: Acceptance is VOLUNTARY
• Say 'Unable' if can't comply
• Must acknowledge clearance with full readback
• Student pilots should not participate

C - Clearance limit (usually destination)
R - Route of flight
A - Altitude (initial/expect)
F - Frequency (departure)
T - Transponder code

Read back ALL clearances completely!

• Authorized to fly route in flight plan
• May still have:
 - Different altitude assignment
 - Departure procedure (SID)
 - Restrictions or amendments

Always read back complete clearance including any modifications

MUST read back:
• Altitudes
• Headings
• Routes
• Hold short instructions
• Runway assignments
• Any clearance to enter/cross runway

NEVER assume - if unclear, ask for clarification!

Allows flight when weather below basic VFR:

Requirements:
• 1 SM visibility minimum
• Clear of clouds
• ATC clearance required
• In controlled airspace surface area

Night SVFR: Pilot instrument rated, aircraft IFR equipped

Some airports prohibit SVFR (see Part 91 Appendix D)

• Squawk 7600
• Continue VFR if possible
• Land at suitable airport
• If at towered airport, watch for light signals
• Rock wings to acknowledge (day)
• Flash landing light (night)

cards.front: Light Gun Signals - Aircraft in Flight
cards.back:
Steady GREEN: Cleared to land
Flashing GREEN: Return for landing
Steady RED: Give way, continue circling
Flashing RED: Airport unsafe, do not land
Flashing WHITE: Not used
Alternating RED/GREEN: Exercise extreme caution

cards.front: Light Gun Signals - Aircraft on Ground
cards.back:
Steady GREEN: Cleared for takeoff
Flashing GREEN: Cleared to taxi
Steady RED: STOP
Flashing RED: Taxi clear of runway in use
Flashing WHITE: Return to starting point
Alternating RED/GREEN: Exercise extreme caution

ROGER: Message received
WILCO: Will comply with instruction
UNABLE: Cannot comply
AFFIRM: Yes
NEGATIVE: No, or that is not correct
STANDBY: Wait, I'll call you
SAY AGAIN: Repeat your message
READ BACK: Repeat for verification
VERIFY: Confirm accuracy

• Comply without delay
• Safety may be involved
• Used in time-critical situations
• Take action NOW
• Query later if needed

Example: 'Turn left immediately!' - just do it

Report:
1. Aircraft identification
2. Position
3. Time
4. Altitude/flight level
5. Type of flight plan
6. ETA next reporting point
7. Name of following reporting point
8. Remarks

Required for non-radar IFR flights

'Leaving [altitude] for [altitude]' - when departing
'Maintaining [altitude]' - level flight
'Climbing/Descending through [altitude]' - in transition

ATC may ask:
'Say altitude' - report current indicated altitude
'Verify altitude' - confirm assigned altitude

• IFR routing between metro areas
• Uses approach control airspace (no center)
• Generally for non-turbojets at/below 10,000
• Good for short flights (<2 hours)
• File 'TEC' in remarks section of flight plan
• Uses existing airways
• Published TEC routes in Chart Supplement

Not required but recommended:
• Provides SAR protection
• File with FSS (phone, online, radio)
• Activate before departure
• CLOSE upon arrival (or SAR starts!)
• Valid for 2 hours after proposed departure

Doesn't provide ATC services

• Participation voluntary for VFR
• Not regulatory airspace class
• Provides sequencing and traffic advisories
• Primary airport is Class D
• Charted with solid black line
• Pilot participation encouraged
• No transponder requirement (unlike Class C)

Listen before transmitting
Think before you key
Be brief and clear
Use standard phraseology
Speak at normal pace
Avoid 'uh' and 'um'
End with callsign if reply expected
Acknowledge with callsign

A-Alpha, B-Bravo, C-Charlie, D-Delta
E-Echo, F-Foxtrot, G-Golf, H-Hotel
I-India, J-Juliet, K-Kilo, L-Lima
M-Mike, N-November, O-Oscar, P-Papa
Q-Quebec, R-Romeo, S-Sierra, T-Tango
U-Uniform, V-Victor, W-Whiskey, X-X-ray
Y-Yankee, Z-Zulu

0-Zero, 1-Wun, 2-Too, 3-Tree
4-Fow-er, 5-Fife, 6-Six, 7-Seven
8-Ait, 9-Nin-er

Altitudes: Digit by digit below 10,000
• 4,500 = 'Four thousand five hundred'
• 10,000+ = 'One zero thousand'

Frequencies: 'Decimal' for point
• 124.85 = 'One two four point eight five'
